items: When you pick a destination, route options are right there: avoid weigh stations, and show fuel, police reports, scales, hazards and live traffic. The choices stay on this phone. No account.

Avoid weigh stations leaves the highway about two miles before each scale and comes back after it. Truck bans, height and weight still apply. If the detour is long, you choose Avoid or Through scale. Open or closed is shown only when a driver reported it.
Starting a trip shows the arrival time, distance and first turn right away. If you are still in the yard, it says Head to route until the truck is on the line.
On a short screen the extra traffic cards tuck in so the map stays visible. Hazard pins and the Me color chips are easier to tap. Lane closed and Road closed use different icons.
The speed limit sign fills in as soon as navigation starts, instead of staying blank until the next GPS update.
Daytime Map key keeps light source labels on its dark card so they stay readable in sunlight.
Daytime (light) screens: small grey text and live/age labels are dark enough to read in sunlight again.
When NYC's live speed feed is down, RigRoute waits and keeps the last speeds instead of asking again every few seconds.
Starting navigation closes the help tour so it never covers the turn banner.
The map credits (i) stays clear of alerts and nav buttons while driving.
Switching language translates live traffic text drawn while the new language was loading.
Spanish: live traffic lines (source, coverage, included in times) are fully translated, and translations refresh right after an update.
Spanish: the TomTom source label in map popups is translated.
Map pins now open their info for VoiceOver, TalkBack and keyboard users too, and every pin is announced as a button with its name.
The ⋮ menu is now a full-width sheet with each label on one line.
The Truck tab shows its icon again.
The map credits button shows a single (i) and sits above your driving buttons.
Lane arrows, traffic cards and alerts now stack under the turn banner instead of hiding behind it.
The Exit button no longer crowds the distance and street name in the windshield view.
Pins that overlap or run off the screen edge are tidied away until you zoom in.
Speed limit never shows a city-street 25 on an expressway: when a road has no posted limit it uses that road's posted limit nearby or the state default for its road type, marked est.
No more false Off NYC truck route warnings just outside the city (Inwood, Lawrence, Elmont), on divided truck routes, or on expressways.
Fixed: with the phone sideways, the live-reports label no longer covers the traffic legend. Your truck's info now says just now instead of a time in the future.
New look, part 1 (Highbeam): a white Where to? bar, round 56px map buttons, a bright Report button, and dark sheets with one green main button. Easier to see at night and easier to hit with a thumb.
Tapping a live traffic icon now also shows when TomTom says it started, plus its description. Fixed the live-reports pill covering the traffic legend with the phone sideways.

Privacy: sharing your location with a friend is now off by default. When you add a friend, RigRoute asks “Share my location with them?” and nothing is sent until you tap Yes. Choices you already made stay the same.
Tap any icon on the map, like a red 🚘, to see what it is (for example Broken-down vehicle), who reported it and how long ago. A new Map key button in More lists every icon.
The phone Back button now closes the open sheet or panel instead of leaving the app.
Fixes: works better offline on iPhone, Arabic and Hebrew text reads the right way, and tapping Send twice sends only once. More of the app is in Spanish.
If you try to vote twice on a pin, or on your own pin, RigRoute now tells you instead of saying thanks.
Tap a hazard pin and choose 👍 Still there or 👎 Not there, no account needed. Pins marked gone by two drivers disappear. Ask RigRoute now knows how to use every part of the app, like adding a stop.

Fixed: HOS buttons now light up the status you tap right away. Fixed: the Multi-stop sheet lines up on iPhone, and the hint matches the Best order button. Your destination stays after a reload. Bigger buttons, and nothing on the map covers the controls.
Hazards you report are shared with every driver again, no account needed. Pins clear themselves after a few hours (a day for closures). Ask RigRoute only counts answers it actually gives.
No account needed, ever: sign-up and sign-in are gone. Everything works right away and your settings stay on this phone. Report a Bug, Ask RigRoute and What's New all work without signing in.
Ask RigRoute can now answer with an AI helper when it is turned on. If the AI is off or busy, it answers from the built-in help. While you drive, answers are read out loud only.
Sign in without a password: get a code by email. Google sign-in shows up as soon as it is turned on.
Ask RigRoute understands more questions.
Truck routes on local streets: long rigs get wider streets with fewer tight turns, and in New York City routes stick to the official truck routes.
Faster route offers: when traffic builds up, RigRoute tells you about a faster truck-safe road. Tap Switch to take it or Keep to stay. It never changes your route by itself.
Fixed a crash when opening Me before the app finished loading.
New tour in plain words. Tap ? and then Show me around to see every part of the app.
Report a Bug / Suggestion in Me, with an Email us button.
Help RigRoute grow (off unless you turn it on): share only your city and state so we can bring help to drivers near you.
Ask RigRoute: type a question in Help and get an answer about the app.
